stem.en: Suppose all the flowers of a type of plant could only self-pollinate. What would most likely happen to its genetic diversity over several generations?

text.en: It would fall, as no new characters come in from other plants

feedback.en: Yes. With no pollen from other plants, generations stay more alike.

text.en: It would rise, as each flower has both of its parents nearby

feedback.en: Self-pollination gives less mixing, not more.

text.en: It would rise, as self-pollinated flowers make more seed each year

feedback.en: Seed number does not create new mixes of characters.

text.en: It would stay the same, as pollen does not carry any characters

feedback.en: Pollen carries the male gamete, so it does pass on characters.

explanation.en: Cross-pollination brings gametes from a different plant, which mixes characters. If only self-pollination happened, no new characters would come in, so diversity would fall over the generations.

hints.en: Where do new mixes of characters come from?
What does cross-pollination bring that self-pollination does not?
